name: Equal Operator
description:
Equal, or equality, sometimes called double equal for the ``==`` operator, is the state of two variables, which contains the same data, after an optional cast to a common type. It is the same as identical, with possible silent type-juggling.

The equal operators are ``==``, ``!=``, ``<>``, and ``<=>``. The ``switch()`` command also uses equal comparisons.
code:
<?php

    var_dump(0 == '0000'); // true
    var_dump(0 == '0');    // false
    var_dump(0 == 0);      // true

?>

citations.name: How do the PHP equality (== double equals) and identity (=== triple equals) comparison operators differ?
